subject: Clarifying retention windows and cross-region log transfers after incident
messages:

To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Ops <security-ops@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions about post-incident log retention and cross-region copies

Hi Laura / Sean,

Thanks for the quick response during the outage last week — appreciate the team's help. Two follow-ups from Acme security:

1) Retention window: what is Redwood's default retention for raw inference request logs and the incident-specific retention period? Our legal team is asking whether we can request a shorter retention for sensitive events.

2) Cross-region copies: did any of the forensic exports or backups get replicated to EU regions (we have strict controls about EU copies for these accounts)? If so, we need details on which buckets/keys and an action plan for containment or deletion.

3) Chain of custody: can you provide your standard chain-of-custody form and the preferred transfer method (S3 pre-signed link vs. direct SFTP vs. SecureAudit handoff)?

Attached our internal evidence request form (acme_chain_of_custody_form.pdf). Please let me know what you can share and timelines — we have a compliance checkpoint on Thursday.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Cho
Security Ops, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: Questions about post-incident log retention and cross-region copies

Michael — thanks for the clear ask and the form. Quick summary while I pull the detailed artifacts:

- Default retention: Redwood keeps raw request/response logs (full, unredacted) for 90 days by default.
- Incident retention policy: for incident investigations we escalate to our IR retention window of 365 days (policy IR-Retention-2026) unless a customer requests an alternative on record.
- Cross-region copies: initial checks indicate no automated EU-region replication for this customer's raw forensic export. There is a nearline backup in us-west-2 created as part of the incident export. I will confirm object paths and whether any manual transfers occurred.

I'll attach our forensic handoff checklist (forensic_checklist_v2.pdf) and coordinate with Vivek and Mina to produce a transfer package and checksums.

Proposed next steps:
- I will produce a short scope memo and list of object URIs by EOD.
- Vivek to confirm whether any snapshots were pushed to other regions or partner accounts.
- If Acme prefers a shorter retention window for this incident, confirm in writing and we can set a scoped data disposition plan with a timeline.

Would you like us to provision a pre-signed S3 handoff, or have SecureAudit pull directly? I can arrange either.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Security Manager
Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions about post-incident log retention and cross-region copies

Laura / Michael — quick technical confirmation from infra:

- Export snapshot: A single forensic snapshot was generated 2028-02-26 22:14 UTC and staged to our secure archive in us-west-2. Filename: incident_log_export_20280226.zip.
- Replication: No automatic cross-region replication was enabled on that export container. I checked replication rules and cross-account ACLs — none were triggered.
- Backups: We do maintain redundant cold backups (tape-backend ledger) but those are UUID-indexed and kept in the same region by policy for this customer.

Options we can offer for handoff:
- Provide S3 pre-signed URLs with time-limited access (recommended) and include MD5 and SHA256 checksums for validation.
- Create a temporary read-only bucket for SecureAudit and configure VPC endpoint access.
- If Acme requires EU residency for certain artifacts, we can execute an in-region copy after obtaining explicit authorization and a formal legal hold request — note that will create an EU copy which then falls under your EU data rules.

Recommended disposition path (default unless Acme requests otherwise):
1) Preserve the staged US export for 180 days (to meet immediate audit needs).
2) Provide checksums and a one-time handoff to SecureAudit via pre-signed URLs within 24 hours of approval.
3) After 180 days, delete the staged export unless an extended hold is requested in writing.

I will prepare the checksums and object URIs and upload them to the Drive folder Laura mentioned.

Vivek Kulkarni
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Thanks — Sarah from SecureAudit. A couple quick requests to make the handoff auditable on our side: 

- Please provide MD5 and SHA256 checksums for incident_log_export_20280226.zip.
- Preferred transfer: pre-signed S3 URLs are fine. We also require an executed chain-of-custody form (we can accept Acme's form or Redwood's).
- For PII considerations: will Redwood redact IP addresses or any customer-supplied PII before handoff, or should we expect raw logs? If redaction is required, please outline the redaction fields and a sample exported record.

Note: if Acme signs a legal hold, SecureAudit can act as escrow and opt to store the evidence in an EU region if requested, but we need written authorization from Acme security to initiate cross-region storage.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call if useful — I have availability today 11:00–13:00 PT.

All — summary and agreed plan below (please reply-all with approval or edits):

1) Preservation window: Redwood will preserve the staged forensic export (incident_log_export_20280226.zip) in us-west-2 for 180 days, effective today (2028-02-28). After 180 days we will schedule deletion unless Acme provides a written extension.

2) Transfer method: We will provision S3 pre-signed URLs for SecureAudit to pull the export. Vivek will include MD5 and SHA256 checksums in the transfer email.

3) PII/redaction: The export contains raw request metadata and redaction-sensitive fields (client IP, user-supplied content). Redwood will produce two artifacts: (a) a redacted CSV for quick review (PII removed), and (b) the full raw export for SecureAudit under the handoff agreement. If Acme requests we redact prior to handoff, we will execute redaction and note the fields removed.

4) Chain of custody: Acme's form was received. Redwood will sign our standard custody form and return a combined COC PDF before transfer. Document will be uploaded to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cIncidentDocs

5) Next actions and owners:
- Vivek: produce pre-signed URLs + checksums and post to Drive (ETA: 24 hours).
- Mina: create redacted CSV sample and list of redaction rules (ETA: 36 hours).
- Laura: coordinate legal/approval and confirm final disposition schedule (180 days) with Acme.

Please confirm by EOD if this plan is acceptable. If Acme prefers an EU-resident escrow, we need written authorization and a short ticket to initiate cross-region copy (this will create an EU copy which falls under your EU obligations).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
